claims.claim: The finite post-H,K endpoint branch remains quarantined: the same-regulator source table and cutoff-uniform tail bound are absent, so no endpoint sign or Clay-level conclusion is licensed.

A viable conceptual frontier is a two-axis physical-sector carrier V_{alpha,p}: alpha controls geometric resolution while p orders actual inclusion of centered gauge-invariant Wilson-net spans on one fixed SU(3) heat-kernel regulator trajectory.

For actually nested V_{alpha,p}, the projected transfer-operator Rayleigh supremum at one fixed physical time t0 is nondecreasing in p, so its physical mass estimate is nonincreasing, provided the actual OS quotient images are nested and use the same transfer contraction. No such monotonicity is inferred from the numerical order of alpha.

Conditionally, a common fixed-time quadratic-form bound on a dense, vacuum-orthogonal recovered union extends to the whole physical sector by continuity. Equivalently, a common exclusion of [0,m) extends because spectral projections are bounded.
Strict regulator-level OS positivity margins are unnecessary; nonnegativity, or a certified vanishing negative defect, together with convergence of reflection forms is the closed-cone condition.
A nonzero OS norm is the minimal anti-vacuity witness. A surviving connected higher cumulant is a separate, stronger non-Gaussian or interacting witness and cannot substitute for density or the gap.
A functional inequality for auxiliary Langevin or sampling dynamics does not constrain the Hamiltonian spectrum without an intertwining theorem; using it directly would be a proxy shift.
No alpha-indexed recovery errors, physical-sector transfer matrices, density residuals, nontriviality witnesses, or common physical mass floor are currently available. The route remains unproved.

A sealed direct-sum calibration has a positive visible-sector gap but a zero full gap, demonstrating that the alpha=1 finite carrier can only falsify or characterize visibility until density is proved.
Sealed finite-volume and noncommuting-limit calibrations show that positive finite-regulator estimates need uniform volume/cutoff control and an explicit order-of-limits theorem.

Fixed-rank recovery obstruction: if M regulated carrier vectors recover coherently to a common continuum Hilbert space, their limit span is closed and has dimension at most M; it cannot be dense when the vacuum-orthogonal physical sector has dimension greater than M.

For the three-channel alpha=1,p=1 carrier, coherent recovery therefore cannot prove density in an infinite-dimensional physical sector, while failure of coherent recovery triggers proxy-shift or noncommuting-limit quarantine. Any viable density route must let inclusion degree p grow.

public_derivation: The support condition gives E_H([0,m))psi=0 for psi in D.
Continuity extends the equality from dense D to Omega-perp.
A common quadratic-form bound for T(t0)=exp(-t0 H) on dense linear D also extends by continuity and yields the same exclusion.
A compressed bound at fixed alpha or for one vector is insufficient.
conditional_lemma.statement: Let H>=0 have vacuum Omega and let D be dense in Omega-perp. If every vector in D has spectral measure disjoint from [0,m) for one common m>0, then E_H([0,m)) vanishes on Omega-perp. This also excludes additional zero-energy states.
conditional_lemma.title: Dense-carrier spectral exclusion

density_quantifier_contract: For every continuum physical vector psi and tolerance epsilon>0, there must exist an inclusion degree p and n0 such that for all n>=n0 a same-theory recovered vector from V_{alpha,p,n} approximates psi within epsilon.

proof_outline: The limits of at most M recovered basis vectors span W.
A span generated by at most M vectors has dimension at most M.
Every finite-dimensional subspace of a Hilbert space is closed.
A proper closed subspace is not dense.
If recovered vectors do not converge coherently, the same-theory recovery gate fails instead.
fixed_rank_obstruction.statement: Let W_n be regulated carrier spaces with dim(W_n)<=M. If their recovered basis vectors converge in one continuum Hilbert space, the recovered limit carrier W has dim(W)<=M and is closed. Thus W is not dense whenever dim(H_physical)>M.
